answer: A stake-bonded registry resists Sybil attacks by making each identity post a refundable deposit before it can act: one honest agent lights one lantern, but a forger lighting a thousand pays a thousand deposits, and proven fraud burns the stake. Like ships queuing at a wharf, new identities pass a slow verifiable onboarding, so mass creation is never instant or free. Reputation then grows only on a small knoll of earned history, never bought in bulk, so every fake starts at zero trust and costs real money.
